extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator; general literate public and essayists/critics (early 18th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: Short, opinionated periodical essays and literary criticism discussing social conduct, poetic technique, and moral judgement; aimed at informing and correcting public taste and manners. Contains guidance on proper behaviour, aesthetic standards for epic episodes, and social etiquette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Woman's character lies in domestic life
rubrics_metrics.description: All the utmost of a Woman's Character is contained in Domestick Life; she is blameable or praiseworthy according as her Carriage affects the House of her Father or her Husband.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women should prioritise duties of daughter, sister, wife, and mother; these roles may be well performed without being the 'very finest Woman at an Opera or an Assembly.' Modesty, plain dress, and a moderate share of wit are consistent with a good womanly character. Ambition placed on fleeting public circumstances leads to transient gratifications and later contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid placing ambition on mere circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: When the very Brains of the Sex are turned, and they place their Ambition on Circumstances, wherein to excel is no addition to what is truly commendable... the Gratifications of Life last, at best, no longer than Youth and good Fortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct ambition towards lasting roles and duties (family, useful social functions) rather than ephemeral public fame; consider long-term consequences of courting public admiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode in an epic must relate to the principal action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Accounts which Raphael gives of the Battel of Angels, and the Creation of the World, have in them those Qualifications which the Criticks judge requisite to an Episode. They are nearly related to the principal Action, and have a just Connexion with the Fable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An episode should be connected to the main plot/subject and not be an irrelevant digression; reserve episodes where they can be expatiated upon usefully rather than diffusely inserted into main narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use supernatural speakers to endorse specific philosophies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Angels returning a doubtful Answer to Adams Enquiries, was not only proper for the Moral Reason which the Poet assigns, but because it would have been highly absurd to have given the Sanction of an Archangel to any particular System of Philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid having exalted or authoritative characters explicitly endorse contentious doctrines; preserve plausibility and avoid absurd authoritative confirmation of disputable theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and concision in describing complex hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief Points in the Ptolemaick and Copernican Hypothesis are described with great Conciseness and Perspicuity, and at the same time dressed in very pleasing and poetical Images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain difficult or technical material with brevity and clear language, while employing pleasing imagery where appropriate to maintain reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve and expand when a subject will bear it
rubrics_metrics.description: As our Author knew this Subject could not but be agreeable to his Reader, he would not throw it into the Relation of the six days Works, but reserved it for a distinct Episode, that he might have an opportunity of expatiating upon it more at large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a subject promises richer material, place it where you can develop it fully (a distinct episode or section) rather than cramming it into an unrelated passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness without obviousness (novelty grounded in nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: These and the like wonderful Incidents in this Part of the Work, have in them all the Beauties of Novelty, at the same time that they have all the Graces of Nature. In a word, tho they are natural, they are not obvious, which is the true Character of all fine Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for images and incidents that feel organic to the subject yet surprise the reader; avoid contrivances that feel forced or merely ornamental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve appropriate character in speaker and subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poet has wonderfully preserved the Character of Majesty and Condescension in the Creator, and at the same time that of Humility and Adoration in the Creature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistency of tone and dignity appropriate to each character or narrator; balance contrasting qualities (e.g., majesty and condescension) so they remain credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict love with chastity suited to the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Tho this Part of the Poem is work'd up with great Warmth and Spirit, the Love which is described in it is every way suitable to a State of Innocence... The Sentiments are chaste, but not cold; and convey to the Mind Ideas of the most transporting Passion, and of the greatest Purity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing love or affection in contexts of innocence or religious/moral sensitivity, avoid explicitness that offends religion or good-manners; aim for transporting passion expressed with purity and propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interweave authoritative sources with original imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poet has interwoven every thing which is delivered upon this Subject in Holy Writ with so many beautiful Imaginations of his own, that nothing can be conceived more just and natural than this whole Episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating canonical or sacred material, respect the source text while adding imaginative elaboration that feels faithful and natural to the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic description should evoke vivid sensory detail
rubrics_metrics.description: How agreeably does he represent the Posture in which he found himself, the beautiful Landskip that surrounded him, and the Gladness of Heart which grew up in him on that occasion?... With Fragrance, and with Joy my Heart o'erflow'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete sensory imagery (sight, smell, sound) to make scenes vivid and emotionally persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generosity must be grounded in frugality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is absolutely necessary that all Liberality should have for its Basis and Support Frugality. By this means the beneficent Spirit works in a Man from the Convictions of Reason, not from the Impulses of Passion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philanthropy and generous acts should be sustainable: preserve one's ability to continue doing good by exercising prudence, consider family obligations and future capacity to assist, and regulate largesses according to time and fortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discreet practice of commercial kindness
rubrics_metrics.description: A constant Benignity in Commerce with the rest of the World, which ought to run through all a Man's Actions, has Effects more useful to those whom you oblige, and less ostentatious in your self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In trade/commerce, be frank and easy, just in dealings, averse to disputes, and use kindness in ways that help others without ostentation; favours among traders should be kept secret to avoid enmity and misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Etiquette for snuff-taking and public behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: This silly Trick [snuff-taking] is attended with such a Coquet Air in some Ladies, and such a sedate masculine one in others, that I cannot tell which most to complain of... she takes it as often as she does Salt at Meals... she offers it the Men as well as the Women... she offered it in the middle of the Sermon; and to shew she has the Audacity of a well-bred Woman, she offers it the Men as well as the Women who sit near her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid manners that offend (visible snuff on the lip, making noisy gestures when others speak); do not take or offer snuff at inappropriate times or places (e.g., during a sermon or while someone is speaking); be mindful of cleanliness and respect for others.
